empirical_demonstrations.name: Roseto Effect
empirical_demonstrations.what_it_demonstrates: Roseto is the candidate case for intense social cohesion suppressing cardiovascular mortality, with the reported advantage over the neighbouring town eroding within a generation as the cohesion broke down. Cor carries it as a hypothesis-generating natural experiment and carries no effect size for it: the source paper is held as page scans with no open-access full text, the design is observational and single-town, and the effect is contested.
empirical_demonstrations.narrative: Roseto, Pennsylvania was a small Italian-American immigrant community with unusually strong intergenerational family structures, tight social cohesion and shared community ritual through the 1950s and 1960s. Stewart Wolf and colleagues reported lower myocardial-infarction mortality there than in the neighbouring town of Bangor despite comparable standard risk factors, and reported that the advantage eroded as the younger generation assimilated. Egolf, Lasker, Wolf and Potvin extended the comparison across 1935 to 1985 to test whether the earlier finding was a small-town fluctuation. Cor carries Roseto as a suggestive natural experiment for the causal role of social scaffolding and carries no number for it: the 1992 paper has no open-access full text, so its mortality figures cannot be quoted verbatim under the extraction standard. The design is observational and single-town, the cohesion measures are retrospective, and the effect is contested in the epidemiological literature. Read this row as a hypothesis-generating case, not as an effect size.
empirical_demonstrations.effect_size: No verbatim-sourced effect size. The 1992 American Journal of Public Health paper (PMID 1636828, PMC1695733) exists in PMC only as page scans with no open-access full text, so no mortality figure is carried. Observational, single-town natural experiment; the effect is contested.
empirical_demonstrations.primary_metric_display: No open-access effect size; observational, single town

empirical_demonstrations.name: SMILES Trial: Diet and Depression
empirical_demonstrations.what_it_demonstrates: A Mediterranean-style dietary intervention brought 32.3% of the dietary arm below the MADRS remission cut against 8.0% of a social-support control over 12 weeks, supporting a causal reading of M13 (energy regulation and diet quality) and M8 (inflammation) in what keeps the low-mood signal firing, rather than treating diet as a correlate. One small unblinded trial, so the direction is better established than the magnitude.
empirical_demonstrations.narrative: Jacka et al. 2017 (BMC Medicine) ran the SMILES randomised controlled trial, comparing a Mediterranean-style dietary intervention against a befriending social-support control in adults diagnosed with moderate-to-severe major depressive disorder. Of 166 assessed for eligibility, 67 were randomised, 33 to diet and 34 to social support. At 12 weeks, 32.3% of the dietary arm and 8.0% of the control arm met remission criteria of a MADRS score below 10, giving a number needed to treat of 4.1 with a wide confidence interval of 2.3 to 27.8. The effect is unusually large for a dietary intervention in a clinical sample, and the trial's own limitations section is the right counterweight: participants could not be blinded, completion differed sharply between arms (94% against 73.5%), the planned sample size was not reached, and the authors say this may have inflated the observed effect. SMILES supports a causal rather than merely correlational reading of the diet and depression link, and it does so as one small unblinded trial. Cor carries no replication claim for it.
empirical_demonstrations.effect_size: At 12 weeks, 32.3% (n=10) of the dietary support group and 8.0% (n=2) of the social support control group reached remission on the MADRS, chi-square(1)=4.84, p=0.028, from 67 adults randomised. Number needed to treat 4.1, 95% CI 2.3 to 27.8. Between-group Cohen's d on the continuous MADRS was 1.16.
empirical_demonstrations.primary_metric_display: 32.3% vs 8.0% remission at 12 weeks (NNT 4.1, 95% CI 2.3 to 27.8)

empirical_demonstrations.name: Captive vs Wild Chimpanzee Abnormality
empirical_demonstrations.what_it_demonstrates: Aversive behavioural outputs in captive primates track environmental mismatch rather than defective design. Every one of the 40 zoo-living chimpanzees studied showed abnormal behaviour, and every one showed at least two distinct types, despite living in social groups in enriched enclosures. The authors' own qualifier travels with the finding: 17 of the 37 catalogued behaviours have been reported to occur rarely in wild chimpanzees, so the claim is that abnormal behaviour is endemic in captivity; it is not a claim that such behaviour is unknown in the wild.
empirical_demonstrations.narrative: Birkett and Newton-Fisher (2011, PLoS ONE) recorded abnormal behaviours through direct focal sampling of 40 adult and adolescent chimpanzees at six accredited zoological institutions, choosing individuals housed in social groups in enriched enclosures because that is the context in which abnormal behaviour should be least likely. Abnormal behaviour was present in every sampled individual and in all six groups, and every individual showed at least two different types. Frequency and duration varied widely and were not explained by sex, age, rearing history or prior housing. A typical individual carried about five abnormal behaviours and spent four to five percent of its activity on them; some exceeded 60 percent. The authors compare this with 1023 hours of focal sampling of wild chimpanzees in Uganda, in which none of the listed behaviours appeared, while noting that 17 of their 37 catalogued behaviours have been reported to occur rarely in the wild and that coprophagy, the most prevalent captive abnormality, is documented in at least six wild populations. Their conclusion is that most captive chimpanzee behaviour is normal in the sense of being seen in wild counterparts, and that abnormal behaviour is endemic in captivity. The hardware works; the environment is wrong.
empirical_demonstrations.effect_size: Abnormal behaviour present in all 40 sampled individuals across six accredited zoological institutions, with every individual showing at least two different types. In 1023 hours of focal sampling of wild chimpanzees in Uganda none of the listed abnormal behaviours were observed, though 17 of the 37 catalogued behaviours have been reported to occur rarely in wild chimpanzees. Single observational study, described by its authors as preliminary.
empirical_demonstrations.primary_metric_display: Abnormal behaviour in all 40 captive chimpanzees sampled

empirical_demonstrations.name: Exercise Trials in Diagnosed Depression
empirical_demonstrations.what_it_demonstrates: In people diagnosed with major depression, exercise lowers depression scores in its own right, beyond any general-health benefit, with modality-specific effect sizes that are moderate and certainty that is low. Randomisation orders the arrow. This supports M10 (movement) as a mechanism in what keeps the low-mood signal firing while keeping the strength of the claim inside what the evidence carries.
empirical_demonstrations.narrative: Noetel et al. 2024 (BMJ) pooled 218 randomised trials of exercise in people diagnosed with major depressive disorder, 495 arms and 14170 participants, in a Bayesian network meta-analysis that compared exercise modalities against each other and against psychotherapy, antidepressants and control conditions. Measured against active controls such as usual care or a placebo tablet, walking or jogging, yoga and strength training all produced moderate reductions in depression scores, with effects proportional to the intensity prescribed and with yoga and strength training the best tolerated. The authors conclude these forms of exercise could be considered alongside psychotherapy and antidepressants as core treatments. The certainty has to travel with the number: only one of the 218 studies met the Cochrane criteria for low risk of bias, so graded confidence was low for walking or jogging and very low for the rest, and the authors call for trials that blind participants and staff. Cor reads this as real support for M10 at a moderate effect size with low certainty, and drops the earlier claim of non-inferiority to SSRIs, which was not sourced. The Schuch 2016 meta-analysis (work 111) is paywalled and no open-access copy was reachable, so it carries no extraction.
empirical_demonstrations.effect_size: Network meta-analysis of 218 randomised trials, 495 arms and 14170 participants. Against active controls, Hedges' g was -0.62 for walking or jogging (95% credible interval -0.80 to -0.45), -0.55 for yoga, -0.49 for strength training, -0.43 for mixed aerobic exercise and -0.42 for tai chi or qigong, with effects proportional to prescribed intensity. Only one included study met Cochrane low-risk-of-bias criteria, so CINeMA confidence was low for walking or jogging and very low for every other modality. The earlier 'Cohen's d ~0.8' and the head-to-head non-inferiority claim have been removed.
empirical_demonstrations.primary_metric_display: Hedges' g -0.62 for walking or jogging vs active control (low certainty)

empirical_demonstrations.name: Chronotherapy in Depression
empirical_demonstrations.what_it_demonstrates: Directly re-timing the circadian and sleep system produces a rapid drop in depression scores (HRSD-6) that is still present six months later, which makes M7 a cascade entry point rather than a downstream symptom. The size of the response is modest and comes from a single pilot trial, so this row demonstrates that the entry point exists and does not establish how large the effect is.
empirical_demonstrations.narrative: Triple chronotherapy combines one bout of total sleep deprivation, a staged advance of sleep timing over the following days, and daily morning bright light, so that the timing architecture is reset directly instead of being approached through mood. Veale et al. 2021 (BJPsych Open) randomised 82 out-patients diagnosed with depression, single blind, to the protocol or to a control of psychoeducation and written information. Response, defined as at least a 50% reduction in symptoms, reached 33.3% in the chronotherapy arm against 16.2% in controls after one week, and held at 35.9% against 13.9% at 26 weeks, with a between-group effect size of 0.8 rising to 1.30. Adherence was high and no adverse effects were reported. Two limits govern how far this goes: the trial was powered for feasibility rather than efficacy, and the comparator was psychoeducation, so nothing here compares chronotherapy with medication. Cor previously sourced this row to the Wirz-Justice and Benedetti clinician's manual (work 113), a book with no DOI, and carried response figures that could not be traced; the row now rests on the one open-access randomised trial reachable in full text.
empirical_demonstrations.effect_size: In a single-blind pilot randomised trial of 82 out-patients diagnosed with depression, a response of at least 50% symptom reduction was achieved by 33.3% of the triple chronotherapy group against 16.2% of controls at week 1, and by 35.9% against 13.9% at week 26. Between-group Cohen's d on the HRSD-6 was 0.8 at week 1 and 1.30 at week 26. The trial's stated primary outcome was feasibility, and the comparator was psychoeducation rather than medication. The earlier '60%+ within a week' and '~30% for pharmacotherapy alone' figures were not traceable to a source and have been removed.
empirical_demonstrations.primary_metric_display: 33.3% vs 16.2% response at 1 week (pilot RCT, n=82)

empirical_demonstrations.name: Forest Troop Culture Change
empirical_demonstrations.what_it_demonstrates: Hierarchy type (not the mere existence of hierarchy) determines pathology, and a troop's social culture is transmissible and reversible within a single generation without genetic turnover.
empirical_demonstrations.narrative: Sapolsky and Share's long-studied olive baboon troop in Kenya lost its most aggressive adult males to a bovine tuberculosis outbreak that began in 1983, after those males monopolised a tourist-lodge garbage dump and ate tubercular meat. All refuse-eating Forest Troop males died, 46% of the adult males, and no other Forest Troop animals did. The deaths more than doubled the female-to-male ratio, to roughly 2:1, and left a disproportionately unaggressive, affiliative set of survivors. By 1993 no adult male remained from the 1983-1986 period, yet the troop's social style persisted: males groomed more, sat in close proximity more, and directed less aggression at females and at males far below them in rank. Overall aggression rates matched the control troops; the distribution is what had shifted. Subordinate males lacked the stress physiology that subordination normally carries, showing neither elevated basal glucocorticoids nor a response to a pharmacological anxiety challenge that reliably affected low-ranking males in the control troop. Resident females, who treated new transfer males affiliatively and unconditionally, appear to carry the transmission. This is a natural experiment on one troop rather than a randomised intervention, and its force comes from the matched control troops rather than from randomisation.
empirical_demonstrations.effect_size: Subordinate Forest Troop 1993-96 males did not show the elevated basal glucocorticoid levels that low-ranking males show in the control troops, and a beta-carboline anxiety challenge raised anxiety-related behaviours in low-ranking control-troop males while leaving low-ranking Forest Troop males unaffected. Forest Troop males also groomed more often and were in close proximity to other animals more often than control-troop males. Overall rates of aggressive interaction did not differ between troops; what changed was the distribution, towards closely ranked dyads and away from females. The paper reports no percentage change for cortisol and none for grooming, so the earlier '30-40% cortisol reduction' and 'grooming roughly doubled' figures have been removed.
empirical_demonstrations.primary_metric_display: Rank-linked stress physiology absent in Forest Troop subordinates

empirical_demonstrations.name: Bucharest Early Intervention Project
empirical_demonstrations.what_it_demonstrates: Early developmental calibration (DA7) depends on the presence of specific social input; institutional care without an alloparental network produces durable brain, attachment, and cognitive deficits that are partially reversible by foster placement but persistently worse than never-institutionalized outcomes.
empirical_demonstrations.narrative: The Bucharest Early Intervention Project (Zeanah, Nelson, Fox and colleagues) randomised institutionalised Romanian children to continued institutional care or to high-quality foster care, and compared both against never-institutionalised community children. The primary metric here is taken from the open-access 2022 PNAS follow-up, which assessed 135 participants in early adulthood at a mean age of 18.74 years: those randomised to foster care scored 9 IQ points higher, 0.6 SD, than those randomised to care as usual, sixteen years after the assignment and long after many participants in both arms had left their original placement. Mediation analyses attribute the effect to the caregiving relationship rather than to placement itself. The gap to the community comparison group remained large: any history of institutional care carried an average deficit of 26.21 full-scale IQ points, with the same direction on every subscale. Early developmental calibration depends on a specific social input, that input is partially restorable, and the restoration is incomplete. The original Science 2007 report (work 108) has no open-access full text and so carries no extraction.
empirical_demonstrations.effect_size: At age 18, sixteen years after randomisation, children randomised to high-quality foster care scored 9 IQ points higher than those randomised to care as usual, a standardised difference of 0.6 SD, in 135 participants. Anyone with a history of institutional care scored on average 26.21 full-scale IQ points below never-institutionalised community comparison participants, so the intervention gain is durable and does not close the deprivation gap. The earlier 'about 2x IQ' and 'attachment disorganisation approximately halved' figures were not traceable to any BEIP publication and have been removed.
empirical_demonstrations.primary_metric_display: Foster care worth 9 IQ points (0.6 SD) at age 18 vs care as usual

empirical_demonstrations.name: Kangaroo Mother Care
empirical_demonstrations.what_it_demonstrates: Skin-to-skin contact between preterm infants and caregivers lowers neonatal mortality, which makes R1 (C-tactile touch as regulatory input to M3) architecture rather than a comfort measure. The mortality result comes from pooled randomised trials in low and middle income settings against routine incubator care, and that scope travels with it.
empirical_demonstrations.narrative: Kangaroo mother care is continuous skin-to-skin contact between a low-birth-weight infant and a caregiver, with support for exclusive breastfeeding and early response to illness, replacing or supplementing incubator care. Lawn et al. 2010 (Int J Epidemiol) reviewed 15 studies reporting mortality or morbidity and pooled the three randomised trials that started the intervention in the first week of life: neonatal mortality fell by 51%, relative risk 0.49, in infants under 2000 g. Three observational studies gave a smaller 32% reduction. The scope is specific and matters: hospital-based care in low and middle income settings, infants under 2000 g, and a comparator of routine incubator care rather than no care at all. Feldman's longitudinal work on maternal-preterm skin-to-skin contact is carried alongside as supporting evidence for the regulatory channel itself, on physiologic organisation and later stress reactivity, and it reports no mortality result; the '~40% mortality reduction' this row previously attributed to it does not appear there. Charpak's 20-year Bogota follow-up is real and relevant but was not reachable in open-access full text, so no number from it is carried here.
empirical_demonstrations.effect_size: Pooled across three randomised trials that began kangaroo mother care in the first week of life, the relative risk for neonatal mortality was 0.49 (95% CI 0.29 to 0.82) against standard care, a 51% reduction (95% CI 18 to 71) in babies under 2000 g, based on 988 infants. Three observational studies gave a smaller 32% reduction. Comparator is routine incubator care in low and middle income settings. The earlier '~40%' figure was not a finding of the work it was attributed to and has been replaced.
empirical_demonstrations.primary_metric_display: 51% lower neonatal mortality (RR 0.49) in infants under 2000 g

empirical_demonstrations.name: Ilardi TLC Protocol for Depression
empirical_demonstrations.what_it_demonstrates: Ilardi's Therapeutic Lifestyle Change protocol restores resolution conditions across several mechanisms at once (movement, light and sleep, social connection, omega-3, anti-rumination). Its response rates are author-reported, from a 2007 conference presentation and a 2009 trade book. No peer-reviewed randomized trial has been published, so the protocol stands as a worked example of multi-mechanism environmental correction, with the peer-reviewed evidence for its component levers carried by ED6, ED7 and ED8.
empirical_demonstrations.narrative: Stephen Ilardi's Therapeutic Lifestyle Change protocol is a six-lever intervention that targets M10 (movement), M7 (sleep and sunlight), M3 (social connection), M8 and M13 (omega-3 and anti-inflammation), and cognitive anti-rumination, and delivers them together rather than one at a time. Its interest to Cor is structural: it targets what the protocol calls depression by changing several inputs at once, which is what the mismatch reading predicts should work, instead of patching the individual. The evidence status is weak and is stated plainly here. The protocol's response figures come from a 2007 conference presentation and Ilardi's 2009 trade book; no peer-reviewed randomized trial of the full protocol has been published, so no effect size is carried. The peer-reviewed evidence for the individual levers sits in ED6 (diet), ED7 (exercise) and ED8 (circadian timing).
empirical_demonstrations.effect_size: No peer-reviewed effect size. Author-reported response rates only (2007 conference presentation; 2009 trade book).

applications.name: AI Alignment
applications.description: Cor is the missing specification under AI alignment. Current alignment approaches treat human preferences as ground truth and train AI systems to satisfy them. But preferences are mechanism outputs - and under mismatch, mechanisms output preferences that point toward more mismatch (more variable-reward apps, more status comparison, more proxy satisfaction). Aligning AI to unverified preferences entrenches the mismatch rather than correcting it. Cor provides three things AI alignment needs: (1) a fourth evaluation axis - matched/mismatched - alongside helpful/harmless/honest; (2) constitutional knowledge of what a human organism needs before asking what it prefers; (3) a test applicable to every AI output: 'Is this creating conditions for real resolution of a mechanism, or is it activating the mechanism without resolving it?' The highest-risk patterns are AI companions (M3 proxy), status/engagement optimization (M5 proxy), and AI sexual/romantic content (M14 proxy) because the mechanisms hijacked are the deepest and most phylogenetically protected.

evaluation_criteria.primary_test: For any AI-generated output or AI-mediated interaction, ask: does this create conditions for real resolution of the human mechanism being engaged, or does it activate the mechanism without providing the resolution conditions?
evaluation_criteria.dunbar_slot_prohibition: Does this AI interaction pattern risk taking a Dunbar slot (a social-bond slot in the user's ~150-person ceiling)? AI must never take a Dunbar slot.
evaluation_criteria.proxy_gradient_placement: For M14 specifically, locate the AI output on the proxy gradient (real partner → attenuated real → partial proxy → pure proxy soft → pure proxy hard). Outputs on the right side of the gradient carry higher mismatch risk by design.
evaluation_criteria.resolution_check_per_mechanism: For each mechanism an AI output engages, can the resolution conditions specified in v2_mechanisms.resolution_conditions actually be satisfied by interaction with this AI? If not, the AI is creating a proxy.

example_outputs: AI companion products fail the resolution-check for M3: the M3 resolution condition is reliable human co-regulation, which an AI cannot supply regardless of conversational quality. Recommendation: AI companions should route toward human connection, never replace it.

Feed-ranking systems that maximize engagement fail the DA4 open-loop test: engagement is wanting (M2) without liking resolution, by construction. Recommendation: rank by retrospective satisfaction, not prospective click-through.

AI-generated sexual content fails the M14 proxy-gradient test at the ZERO end: no pair bond, no reproductive consequence, maximum hijacking of the LUST circuit. Recommendation: age-gated is insufficient; the architectural risk is intrinsic to the modality.

applications.name: Environment Design
applications.description: Architecture, urban planning, office design, product design, school design, and healthcare facility design currently proceed without a clear account of what the human organism requires to function. Cor provides the framework. Each evolved mechanism has resolution conditions (documented in Cor's mechanism architecture) that the designed environment either satisfies or degrades. The application: design environments that satisfy resolution conditions for each mechanism - M7 light/dark cycles, M10 movement integration, M3 social density, M4 unstructured play space for children, M9 alloparental-care commons, R1 touch-positive cultures. Designers should be able to audit any proposed environment against the Cor inventory and flag which mechanisms will be compromised by default.

evaluation_criteria.reversibility_check: When environmental correction is applied to a previously degraded space, how quickly does mechanism function recover? Design for rapid restoration paths.
evaluation_criteria.cascade_entry_points: Which mechanisms does this environment force into DA8 cascade entry? (e.g., open-plan office degrading M1 via constant threat monitoring, M6 via bureaucratic agency loss, M7 via inconsistent light.)
evaluation_criteria.default_path_analysis: What do occupants do by default in this environment? Does the default path degrade or satisfy mechanism resolution conditions? (Environments design defaults, and defaults design behavior.)
evaluation_criteria.mechanism_satisfaction_audit: For each mechanism M1-M14 + R1, does the designed environment satisfy, degrade, or ignore its resolution conditions? Rate each on a matched / attenuated / mismatched scale.

example_outputs: Office redesign: mandatory outdoor 30-minute walk windows built into the workflow serve M10 and M7 simultaneously; a ~150-person Dunbar ceiling for team/floor structure serves M3 and M5.
Apartment complex: shared alloparental-care commons with multiple trusted caregivers cycling through serves M9 and M3 for families without biological kin nearby.

School design: outdoor unstructured free-play time of ≥90 min/day serves M4 directly; classroom light with morning daylight exposure serves M7; staff-to-student ratios calibrated to attachment capacity serve M3.

applications.name: Policy and Governance
applications.description: Governance currently evaluates policy by economic metrics and preference aggregation. Both are defective evaluation axes: economic metrics measure proxies (GDP, employment) rather than organism-level flourishing; preference aggregation treats mismatched preferences as ground truth. Cor provides a human-organism evaluation axis: does this policy satisfy or degrade mechanism resolution conditions for the population? Applied to food policy (M13 resolution conditions vs ultra-processed food availability), urban design (M3 social density, M10 walkability, M7 light-pollution, M4 child play space), work regulation (M6 agency, M7 shift-work protection, M10 movement integration), digital platform regulation (DC2 engagement-based hijacking of M5 and M14), and environmental policy (M7 circadian disruption from light pollution, M8 air quality). A policy that degrades mechanism resolution conditions is costly regardless of its economic or preference-aggregation scores.

evaluation_criteria.architectural_honesty: Does the policy treat humans as the evolved organism they are, or as economic agents / cultural constructs / blank slates? Evaluate against P2 (domain-sensitive organism) rather than current economic-agent assumptions.
evaluation_criteria.proxy_vs_resolution_design: Does the policy create or remove proxies? Policies that remove industrial proxy exploitation (ultra-processed food, variable-reward apps targeted at children, engagement-metric-maximizing platforms) correct mismatch; policies that subsidize proxies entrench it.
evaluation_criteria.population_mechanism_impact: For each mechanism, how does this policy affect the population's resolution-condition satisfaction? (Net direction + magnitude + vulnerable-subpopulation disparities.)
evaluation_criteria.subpopulation_vulnerability: Which subpopulations are operating with the most degraded mechanism resolution conditions currently? Policy should target the bottleneck mechanisms for those populations first.

example_outputs: Food policy: tax ultra-processed food (M13 proxy bypass of satiety), subsidize whole-food access in low-income areas, regulate marketing to children. Target: M13 and M8 via M13.

Urban design: walkable neighborhoods with third-place social infrastructure serve M3 + M10 + M11 simultaneously; dark-sky ordinances protect M7 for the population; universal child-play spaces serve M4.

Platform regulation: engagement-metric-maximizing algorithms targeted at minors fall under DC2 proxy exploitation and should face the same regulatory treatment as other proxy-exploitation industries. Age-of-access and algorithmic transparency are architectural not values-based issues.

applications.name: Personal Assessment and Self-Understanding
applications.description: Individuals currently diagnose themselves through the cultural filter of psychiatric categories, productivity culture, wellness trends, or self-help frameworks. Cor provides a direct assessment: which mechanism's resolution conditions are unmet in your life right now? A tool built on the framework lets the user answer questions about their environment and get back a picture of which mechanisms are matched vs mismatched, with resolution-condition statements they can act on. This is not therapy, not diagnosis, not productivity advice; it is an audit of the inputs the user's evolved architecture currently is or is not receiving.

evaluation_criteria.one_lever_test: If the user could change one input this week, which mechanism's resolution condition has the highest leverage? (Often M7 or M10 because they unblock cascades.)
evaluation_criteria.proxy_identification: Which resolution conditions is the user currently meeting via proxy rather than via matched input? (e.g., M5 satisfied via social media status metrics is a proxy; M5 satisfied via a trusted ~150-person reference group is matched.)
evaluation_criteria.cascade_identification: Are there active cross-mechanism cascades (e.g., M3 deficit → M1 elevated → M2 suppressed → M10 reduced → M8 inflammation)? The dashboard should surface these patterns.
evaluation_criteria.mechanism_state_self_report: For each mechanism, the user reports the current state of its resolution conditions (satisfied, partial, absent).

example_outputs: Individual dashboard output: M3 (8 co-regulators, physical presence weekly) matched; M7 (sleep fragmented, blue-light exposure until late) mismatched; M10 (sedentary, 2000 steps/day) severely mismatched; M5 (social-media status comparison with millions) proxy-satisfied. Priority: M10 and M7 simultaneously (break the M10-M7-M8 cascade chain).

Audit for a new parent: M9 (no alloparental network, 0 trusted co-caregivers sharing load) severely mismatched, driving M7, M3, and M1 all into cascade. Priority: build alloparental network; this is the architectural rather than the cultural frame.

Audit for a remote worker: M3 (mediated contact only), M6 (abstract work without visible action-outcome feedback), M10 (sedentary), M7 (no consistent light cue) all mismatched. Remote work is an architectural risk profile, not a lifestyle preference.

applications.name: AI Training Data Curation
applications.description: Pretraining data is AI environment. The spec evaluates any training corpus against mechanism resolution conditions.

applications.name: Augmentation Ethics
applications.description: Neural interfaces, pharmacological modulators, and closed-loop implants reach inside the evolved architecture. Without the spec, augmentation silences signals without addressing what they protect.

applications.name: Education and Child Development
applications.description: Current education treats children as cognitive agents to fill with information, organized around the economic value of the adult they will become. Cor reframes education as organism care: children are developing organisms with mechanism requirements that current school design routinely violates. M4 (play) requires unstructured, unsupervised physical play with other children (in forager childhoods, a mixed-age group), which contemporary schooling systematically removes. M7 (circadian) requires age-appropriate school start times and daylight exposure - routinely violated for adolescents. M10 (movement) requires embedded daily movement, not scheduled PE. M3 (attachment) requires stable caring relationships with specific adults - eroded by class-rotation designs. M9 (alloparenting) assumes children will be cared for by multiple trusted adults - which school + family-only models fail to provide. Educational reform under Cor begins by auditing the design against the mechanism inventory and redesigning to satisfy the resolution conditions of the developing organism.

evaluation_criteria.movement_embedding: Is movement embedded in the default school day, or is it a scheduled add-on? Embedded beats scheduled for M10 resolution.
evaluation_criteria.play_deprivation_audit: How many minutes/day of unstructured, unsupervised physical play with other children, older and younger included, does the child have? (Benchmark: ≥90 min/day for children under 12; current average in many countries is <30 min.)
evaluation_criteria.adult_attachment_stability: How many trusted, stable adult relationships does the child have inside the school? (Cor's M3 prediction: children need multiple, not one, and stability across years matters.)
evaluation_criteria.developmental_window_respect: For each developmental window (M3 attachment, M4 play, M7 sleep timing, M9 alloparenting), does the educational environment provide the inputs that developmental calibration depends on?

example_outputs: School start time policy: adolescent school start times before 8:30 AM systematically violate M7 during a developmental calibration window, producing measurable cognitive and emotional deficits. Evidence-based start times are ≥8:30 AM.
Recess and play policy: ≥90 min/day of unstructured outdoor play for primary school children; play leaders as facilitators not supervisors; no academic substitution.

Teacher stability and ratio: each child has stable access to ≥3 trusted adult educators across their primary years; adult-to-child ratios calibrated to attachment capacity rather than cost-minimization.

applications.name: Clinical Practice
applications.description: Current psychiatry classifies many aversive presentations as disorders and treats them with suppression (pharmacotherapy, CBT targeting the experience). Cor applies the clear-defect rule (DA1). Only a clear physical defect is a disease, whether a test has found it yet or not: an infection, autoimmune encephalitis, a tumour, poisoning, a substance or medication effect, dementia, brain injury. Where such a defect is the cause, it is the sole cause, the behaviour is its symptom, and the defect is treated. A marker is something else. A receptor, a gene variant or a scan pattern that shows how sensitive a person is to stimuli and to mismatch is no defect and no cause, and measured activation can itself sit downstream of mismatch. Where no defect is the cause, there is no disease and Cor uses no disease or disorder wording: the presentation is a normal human response to a mismatched world. The architecture is working correctly, the environment is outside the expected range, heritable sensitivity sets how easily the person tips and how large the response is, and the signal tells the clinician where to look. No label is carved out. Psychosis, bipolar and depression are each applied to cases on both sides of the line, so the first question is whether a clear defect is the cause. Psychosis where no defect is the cause is, on Cor's reading, a signal with no resolution, turned all the way up. In a mismatched world most signals get no resolution, so they keep rising and stop looking like healthy signals. Where a signal gets its answer, as in the world humans lived in for most of their history, it is resolved long before it reaches that level. This is Cor's position and a reading; no study has measured it. Clinical practice redesigned around Cor includes: (1) a search for a clear physical defect, then an environmental audit against the mechanism inventory (M1-M14 + R1), before or alongside symptom treatment, (2) resolution-condition restoration as the first-line intervention where feasible, (3) medication on the clear-defect rule. Where a defect is the cause, the drug may be treating a disease, and treatment follows the medicine for that defect. Where no defect is the cause, the line is the same on every medication page, and it leads with replacement: "The drug gets replaced by the real thing, such as people who need you and give back. The real thing is hard to build under the influence, so the drug comes down while the real thing comes in. Tapering is not a rule for every medication. Where stopping suddenly is biologically dangerous, as with certain drugs and with alcohol, never stop suddenly, and do it with a doctor." Where no defect is the cause, the only imbalance is the one the drug makes, and what is called relapse after stopping is the original signal returning plus withdrawal. A blunted signal also blunts the pain that points at what to fix, which is a second reason the drug comes down while the real thing is built. Where the passivity default (M6) is locked so hard that the person cannot act at all, some lift may come first. The line always travels whole: no coming off without the replacement and the sudden-stop warning, and no warning in place of the replacement. A sudden stop is dangerous with these drugs: abrupt benzodiazepine withdrawal can cause seizures, stopping lithium abruptly raises the risk of relapse and suicide, and antidepressant withdrawal can be severe. The discontinuation trials Cor holds as challenge records took the drug away and put nothing real in its place, so they do not test this line. No trial has tested it.

evaluation_criteria.mechanism_audit: For each presenting symptom, which mechanism(s) is it a signal from? Which resolution conditions are currently unmet?
evaluation_criteria.category_distinction: Is a clear physical defect the cause (an infection, autoimmune encephalitis, a tumour, poisoning, a substance or medication effect, dementia, brain injury), whether a test has found it yet or not? If yes, the behaviour is a symptom of that disease and the defect is treated. A marker that only shows sensitivity to stimuli and to mismatch (a receptor, a gene variant) is no defect, and activation can sit downstream of mismatch. If no defect is the cause: which mechanism is signalling, which resolution has it been missing, what sets its threshold (heritable sensitivity, DA10; developmental calibration, DA7), and is a coupled loop keeping it running after the trigger has passed (DA3)? Treatment differs in each case.
evaluation_criteria.environment_vs_organism: Can the environment be corrected? If yes, try that first: it is the less invasive and more durable intervention.
evaluation_criteria.proxy_versus_resolution: Are current interventions (pharmacological or behavioral) providing resolution or only attenuating the signal? A proxy that attenuates without resolving maintains the underlying mismatch.

example_outputs: Low mood where no physical defect is the cause, in a person with poor sleep, sedentary work and isolated living: a mechanism audit (M7, M10, M3) names the unmet inputs, and the work starts on them. Ilardi's TLC protocol (ED5) targets these same inputs. If the person takes an antidepressant, the drug gets replaced by the real thing: people who need the person and give back, with sleep and movement restored. That is hard to build under the influence, so the dose comes down while the real thing comes in. Antidepressant withdrawal can be severe, so the drug is never stopped suddenly and the dose comes down with a doctor. Expect the low mood to come back as the dose drops: that is the original signal returning plus withdrawal. Go slower when it does.

Panic attacks that start after a period of sleep deprivation have M7-driven amygdala hyperreactivity as the likely driver (Walker). Treatment: sleep restoration. Long-term benzodiazepine use quiets the signal and leaves the sleep loss in place. Where one is already in use, restored sleep replaces it: the dose comes down with a doctor while the sleep comes back, slower if the panic returns as the dose drops. A benzodiazepine is never stopped suddenly, because abrupt benzodiazepine withdrawal can cause seizures.

Adolescent anxiety in a high-device, low-movement, low-outdoor context may be M7, M10 and M4 deprivation expressing as M1 over-activation. The work starts on sleep, movement, daylight and free play with other children. A prescription started before that audit quiets the signal and leaves its source in place. Where one is already in use, those real things replace it, and the dose comes down while they come in. An antidepressant is never stopped suddenly, and the dose comes down with a doctor.

A first psychotic state. First comes the search for a clear physical defect: an infection, autoimmune encephalitis, a tumour, a substance or medication effect. Where one is the cause, the person is sick and the defect is treated. Where none is the cause, Cor reads the state as a signal with no resolution, turned all the way up. That is Cor's position, a reading no study has measured. The audit then asks which signals have had no answer, and for how long: sleep (M7), people (M3), threat (M1). The work starts there: sleep restored, the person's own people around them, the threat ended where it can be. If an antipsychotic is in use, the drug gets replaced by the real thing, such as people who need the person and give back. The real thing is hard to build under the influence, so the dose comes down while the real thing comes in. Tapering is not a rule for every medication. Where stopping suddenly is biologically dangerous, as with certain drugs and with alcohol, never stop suddenly, and do it with a doctor. Expect the state to press back as the dose drops: that is the original signal returning plus withdrawal. Go slower when it does. No trial has tested this replacement. In the trial that reduced the dose with nothing put in its place, severe relapse was about twice as common within two years (ext 1778).

bridge_theses.name: Panksepp-Barrett Resolution
conflicting_frameworks: Panksepp basic emotions (subcortical affective systems as natural kinds)
Barrett theory of constructed emotion (no emotion natural kinds; emotions are constructed)
bridge_theses.resolution:
Barrett's challenge is stronger than a disagreement about emotion categories. She attacks three pillars of the classical view: (1) dedicated emotional brain regions do not exist - every region claimed as a home of emotion is actually a body-budgeting region within the interoceptive network; (2) emotions are not natural kinds - no consistent neural, autonomic, or facial fingerprint has been found for any single emotion category despite a century of search; (3) the brain is predictive, not reactive - it constructs experience through prediction and correction rather than responding to triggering stimuli via dedicated circuits. Barrett replaces the reactive-modular architecture with a predictive-constructive one grounded in interoception and body-budget regulation.

What survives Barrett's critique: Panksepp's conserved subcortical motivational circuitry is real. Cross-species electrical stimulation, lesion, and pharmacological evidence demonstrates that SEEKING, FEAR, RAGE, CARE, PANIC/GRIEF, PLAY, and LUST systems exist as identifiable neural networks with conserved neuroanatomy and neurochemistry across all mammals. These are not folk-emotion categories but motivational-affective systems identified via the triangulation method (human self-report + animal brain manipulation + natural behavior).

The resolution: Panksepp's circuits exist but do NOT map one-to-one onto vernacular emotion categories. The subcortical systems are motivational substrates - they generate valenced states that the brain then constructs into culturally specific emotional experiences via the predictive-interoceptive process Barrett describes. The specification uses Panksepp's systems as mechanism substrates (M1-M14), not as emotion labels. What people experience as 'anger' or 'sadness' is a constructed category that may recruit multiple subcortical systems in different combinations on different occasions - exactly as Barrett's population thinking predicts.

Barrett forces an explicit structural acknowledgment: the interoceptive-predictive layer (body budgeting, allostatic regulation, prediction error processing) is not merely distributed across M1-M14 but constitutes its own architectural level. The specification currently harvests this layer through individual mechanism descriptions but does not name it as a unified process. Whether this warrants a dedicated structural home (a 'body-budget regulation' foundation or meta-mechanism) or remains an emergent property of the mechanism interactions is an open architectural question that the evidence base now supports asking.

eea_parameters.name: Sex and conception coupled
eea_parameters.eea_baseline: For foragers, sex led to pregnancy unless breastfeeding or low energy suppressed ovulation. Birth spacing of 3 to 4 years came from breastfeeding and the energy cost of lactation (EEA-MATE-05).
eea_parameters.modern_default: Contraception separates sex from conception. In 2019, 47.7% of all women aged 15 to 49 worldwide used a modern method, 20.1 points more than in 1970, from 1.9% in South Sudan to 87.9% in Norway. In the US, the pill sped up the fall in marital fertility in the 1960s.
eea_parameters.gap_statement: Sex no longer signals possible children. The motivation system that rewards sex runs as before, while the number of children is now set by a separate decision.
eea_parameters.confidence_note: Grade, rubric v2 (11 Nov 2026): tested many times for modern use levels (Haakenstad et al. 2022, 1,162 surveys). The size of contraception's effect on fertility is one natural experiment (Bailey 2010, thin; the 40% share is the author's own rough counterfactual). Lactational suppression: Ellison 2003 (ext 875), a review; McNeilly 2002 argues that suckling, not energy load, sets how long it lasts. Both agree that breastfeeding suppresses ovulation. In two prospective studies, fully breastfeeding women without periods who used no contraception had pregnancy rates of about 1 percent in the first six months after birth (Van der Wijden and Manion 2015). Background-tier evidence cited (abstract or book only): ext 875.

evidence.author_quote: Between 1970 and 2019, the global mCPR increased by 20·1 percentage points

eea_parameters.name: Membership turnover (camp dissolves and reconstitutes; most campmates change between survey waves)
eea_parameters.eea_baseline: The residential group (camp/band) was a fission-fusion structure that continuously dissolved and reconstituted rather than a fixed-membership unit. Among the best-studied foragers (Hadza), entire camps relocated roughly every 4-8 weeks and individuals reshuffled across camps such that only a minority of campmates carried over from one survey wave to the next (Smith et al. 2018, Hadza waves 1 to 3 years apart; the exact proportion is unverified, see eea_value). Crucially, despite this high residential churn, assortment on cooperation persisted (cooperators clustered together across reshuffles), and what was conserved across the turnover was not the group but the durable, individually-tracked reciprocal relationships between specific people. Group composition was fluid; the dyadic ties were the stable substrate.

eea_value.source: Smith et al. 2018, Current Biology, doi 10.1016/j.cub.2018.07.064 (Hadza; survey waves 2010, 2013, 2014, 2016); in Cor as core work 116
eea_value.repeated_campmates_status: UNVERIFIED: the published Current Biology text has not been read. The two preprint versions disagree because they define the measure differently: bioRxiv 313064v1 reports 12.1% (people lived with at both waves divided by all unique people lived with at either wave); v2 reports 21.9% (share of campmates at one wave still living with the person at the next). Waves are 1 to 3 years apart, so neither is an annual rate.

eea_parameters.modern_default: Modern social environments invert the structure: the GROUP labels are stable and durable (a workplace, a school cohort, a neighborhood, a social-media platform or feed) while the actual dyadic relationships within them are shallow, interchangeable, and disposable. People remain nominal members of named, persistent groups for years, yet cycle through co-members with little individual reciprocal investment, and there is no institution analogous to a delayed-reciprocity partnership (e.g. hxaro) that conserves a specific bond once physical proximity ends. Relationships routinely lapse the moment shared context (job, class, proximity) is removed.
eea_parameters.gap_statement: The ancestral and modern environments are inverted on which layer is stable. Ancestrally the GROUP churned (most campmates changed between survey waves) while the durable reciprocal DYAD was conserved across the churn; the relationship, not the group, was the unit that persisted. Modernity delivers the opposite: stable, durable group labels (workplace, cohort, feed) paired with shallow, disposable dyads and no mechanism (no hxaro-equivalent) for conserving a specific bond once proximity ends. The mismatch lies in where turnover lands: on the relationships, which evolved to persist, instead of on group membership, which evolved to be fluid. That leaves the co-regulating, reputation-tracking reciprocal dyad chronically unmet.
eea_parameters.resolution_unit: The durable reciprocal dyad - a specific, individually-known partner with whom reciprocity, co-regulation, and reputation are tracked over years. What needs conserving across membership turnover is not the group or the amount of contact but the persistence of particular bonded relationships; the bond, not the band, is the conserved unit.
eea_parameters.confidence_note: Smith et al. 2018 (Hadza; ext 602). The preprint figures (12.1% in v1, 21.9% in v2) use different definitions, and the published figure has not been read. Survey waves are 1 to 3 years apart, so neither figure is an annual rate. Single Hadza population.

evidence.author_quote: Across the three intervals, the mean proportion of repeated campmates was 12.1%.
evidence.content: Across 6 years / 4 waves, Hadza camps continuously dissolve and reconstitute: of all the people a person lived with at either of two successive survey waves, only about 12% lived with them at both (waves 1 to 3 years apart), yet cooperative assortment persists.

eea_parameters.name: Band / camp size (a few dozen adults; ~25-50)
eea_parameters.eea_baseline: Ancestral humans lived in small, residentially co-present foraging bands (camps): a single overnight camp typically held on the order of a few dozen adults - roughly 25 to 50, with central estimates clustering near ~28-35 - a scale that sits within the Dunbar 'band' layer (~35) and 'overnight camp' layer (~50) of the nested social network. At this scale every co-resident is a personally known, named individual whose behaviour can be directly observed and tracked over time. Band size was thus bounded well below the ~150 active-network ceiling, keeping the day-to-day social field small enough that cooperation, status, and bonding all operated face-to-face among mutually familiar people rather than among anonymous strangers.

eea_value.units: co-resident adults in a single band / overnight camp
eea_value.source_status: Band about 35 (Dunbar 1998, ext 490) and overnight camp about 50 (Dunbar 2010, ext 404). Median residential group of 27 people across 263 forager societies (Marlowe 2005, ext 754). The mean of 28.2 adults across 32 societies is attributed to Hill et al. 2011 (work 172); Cor's extraction from that work (ext 683) covers relatedness and does not carry the figure.

eea_parameters.modern_default: Modern humans do not live in a single bounded, personally-known residential band. Daily life is partitioned across many large, partly anonymous groupings - workplaces, apartment buildings, transit systems, schools, and online networks - most of which exceed the ~25-50 face-to-face band scale and many of which exceed the ~150 ceiling entirely. A person routinely shares physical or digital space with hundreds or thousands of unfamiliar individuals while their actual co-regulating relationships shrink. The small, stable, fully-known co-resident group of a few dozen adults has no direct modern equivalent; its functions are split across institutions where most co-present others are strangers.
eea_parameters.gap_statement: The ancestral social field was a small set of a few dozen (~25-50) personally-known adults sharing a camp, sitting within the band/overnight-camp Dunbar layer. The modern default replaces this with chronic immersion in groupings far larger than the band scale, dominated by unfamiliar people, while genuinely co-regulating relationships number far fewer than the band once held. The delta is a mismatch between the scale at which our cooperation, status-monitoring, and bonding machinery was calibrated (a bounded, fully-known band/camp of a few dozen adults) and the scale we actually inhabit (large, partly anonymous aggregations plus a thin set of disposable ties), so the band-sized layer that once carried daily social life is no longer delivered by any single modern structure.
eea_parameters.confidence_note: Grade, rubric v2 (6 Nov 2026): tested many times. Residential group size is measured across many forager societies: Marlowe 2005 (263 societies, median 27 people of all ages) and Hill et al. 2011 (32 societies, mean 28.2 adults). The range is wide (13 to 250 people across Marlowe's 263 societies, ext 754); Singh and Glowacki 2022 (ext 756) argue that larger, settled non-agricultural groups also existed in the Late Pleistocene.

evidence.content: Hadza camp size centers near 30 individuals, composed of several unrelated nuclear families.
In 32 present-day forager societies, most members of a residential band were not close genetic kin of one another.

Most mobile hunter-gatherers live in groups dominated by links between non-relatives, where residential group membership is fluid and supports large-scale social networks of interaction

Foragers range from small mobile bands to large settled societies with ranks and stored food, so no single foraging type describes them all.
In Marlowe's cross-cultural sample of foragers, the median residential group size was 27 people (mean 41.4, range 13 to 250, across 263 societies).

evidence.content: !Kung camps were highly crowded, and the !Kung showed no biological indicators of stress from it.

eea_parameters.name: Novel-stranger frequency (rare, salient, often a threat)
eea_parameters.eea_baseline: Social cognition operated over a bounded pool: a personally-known reference network capped near the ~150 Dunbar ceiling, nested in ~5/15/50/150 layers of decreasing intimacy, the outermost being the people one recognizes and interacts with across a year. Within that architecture almost every face encountered was already known, placed, and reputationally tracked. A genuinely novel stranger - an individual who could not be located anywhere in one's known network or in the known networks of one's allies - was therefore a comparatively rare event. Because the bounded pool had no slot for such a person, novelty itself was diagnostic: a never-before-seen individual could not be vouched for, had no shared reputational history, and could not be assumed to be bound by the local web of reciprocity and norm enforcement. Encounters with unplaceable strangers were thus both infrequent and highly salient, and the threat-management system (M1) treated unfamiliarity as a plausible danger cue to be resolved (placed, vouched-for, or avoided) rather than as a routine background condition. This is an inference from the bounded-pool architecture plus M1, not a directly measured ancestral rate.
eea_parameters.modern_default: The contemporary environment delivers a near-continuous stream of novel, unplaceable faces: dense urban crowds, transit, commerce, and especially the feeds and follower graphs of online platforms expose a person to more unfamiliar individuals in a single day than an ancestral forager might meet in a lifetime. Unfamiliarity is the modal condition rather than the rare exception, so the diagnostic value of novelty collapses - a stranger is no longer informative about anything. Yet the same M1 machinery still treats unplaceable others as potential threats, now firing against a constant baseline it was never calibrated for, while the reputational and vouching scaffolding that once resolved a stranger encounter is largely absent.
eea_parameters.gap_statement: The delta is one of base rate and resolvability. Ancestrally, novel strangers were rare, salient, and resolvable (place them in the known web, or treat unfamiliarity as an actionable threat signal); modernity inverts this to constant, non-diagnostic, unresolvable novelty. The threat-management system inherited from the rare-stranger regime cannot down-regulate to the new base rate: it either over-fires (chronic low-grade vigilance, stranger-directed wariness in crowds and online) or, where it habituates, leaves people transacting with a stream of others who carry none of the reputational accountability the system implicitly assumes. The conserved unit being eroded is not the count of strangers but the durable, reputationally-tracked dyad against which any new face used to be evaluated; once almost everyone is a stranger, the bounded-pool premise that made novelty meaningful no longer holds.
eea_parameters.resolution_unit: The durable, reputationally-tracked reciprocal dyad: ancestrally every new face was evaluated against a finite web of known, vouched-for relationships, and it was that web of bonds - not the count of strangers per se - that gave novelty its diagnostic and protective meaning. The mismatch resolves only insofar as new encounters can be anchored back into durable, accountable relationships rather than left as anonymous one-off contacts.
eea_parameters.confidence_note: Grade: argued, not yet tested. No study measures how often ancestral humans met strangers. The premise is a bounded pool of personally known people in nested layers of about 5, 12, 35 and 150 (Dunbar 1998, ext 490), with a limit on how many relationships a person can monitor at once (Dunbar 1992, ext 485). For the stranger-as-threat side: in chimpanzees, lethal raids by males from neighbouring groups are a major cause of death (Hrdy 2009, ext 383), and across 18 communities most killings were by males and of members of other communities (Wilson et al. 2014, ext 671). This is animal evidence. Ambush killing between groups is documented in several nomadic forager societies, and how often it happened is disputed (Wrangham & Glowacki 2012, ext 672; Bowles 2009, ext 673). Infants show wariness toward an approaching stranger in lab studies (Waters et al. 1975, ext 676). Against it: in 21 mobile forager bands most recorded killings were homicides, a few were feuds and a minority were war (Fry & Söderberg 2013, ext 674), and Tomasello describes cooperation with in-group strangers (Tomasello 2014, ext 238, 250). Bowlby's claim that strangers are an innate fear cue (ext 574) comes from a book that was not read directly and is not linked as evidence.

eea_parameters.name: Alloparental care supply (a village, not a dyad)
eea_parameters.eea_baseline: Ancestral human infants were not raised by a mother alone but by a network of allomothers - fathers, grandmothers, aunts, older siblings, and trusted non-kin - who shared both direct care (holding, carrying, soothing) and provisioning (food). Humans are a cooperatively breeding ape: unlike other African apes, whose mothers nurture infants essentially on their own, hominin mothers relied on groupmates to protect, care for, and provision their unusually slow-maturing, costly young. This is part of human biology: a human child requires on the order of 13 million calories from birth to independence, and humans breed faster (every 3-4 years) than chimpanzees and orangutans (about every 5.5 and 7.7 years; gorillas breed about every 3.8 years, Galdikas and Wood 1990, ext 3519) while producing larger, slower-maturing babies - a life-history paradox solvable only by shared provisioning. Across foraging ethnography, infants were routinely handled by people other than the mother from shortly after birth: among the Hadza, the mother does roughly 69% of the time children aged four and under were held (ext 2128) and allomothers the rest; !Kung infants have the mother's entire social world available with intense face-to-face engagement; Trobriand infants are suckled by lactating allomothers. The infant's evolved expectation is a reliable surround of multiple invested caregivers, not a single isolated dyad.

eea_value.note: Specific aggregate 'alloparent count ~4+' and a generic '40-50% of care delivered by allomothers' figure are widely cited in the literature but are NOT verbatim-grounded in Cor's extractions; only the Hadza ~69/31 mother/allomother holding split and the qualitative multi-caregiver pattern are. Numbers given are the extraction-supported anchors, not an asserted universal mean.

other_ape_interbirth_interval_years.source: median birth intervals in the wild, Galdikas and Wood 1990, ext 3519

eea_parameters.modern_default: The modern default is the isolated nuclear (often single-caregiver) household: one or two adults, frequently without resident grandmothers, aunts, older cousins, or trusted neighbours sharing the daily load. The idealized breadwinner-father / homemaker-mother / biological-children unit is a historical aberration roughly a century old (Victorian at most; the 1950s template in the US), departing from the extended-kin allomaternal norm that held for the vast majority of human history. Care that was distributed across many hands is now concentrated on one or two, often supplemented by paid, rotating, or institutional caregivers rather than a stable invested kin network.
eea_parameters.gap_statement: The mismatch is between the reliable, present, multi-caregiver surround the infant's attachment and the mother's reproductive psychology evolved to expect, and the thin one- or two-adult household the modern environment supplies. The load that was carried by a village now falls on isolated parents; maternal investment is calibrated to assess available allomaternal support (M9), so its evolved absence produces overload, depleted caregivers, and infants with fewer attachment figures than the cooperative-breeding design assumes. This is a supply mismatch, not a parental-competence failure.
eea_parameters.resolution_unit: Reliable, present alloparental supply - care plus provisioning actually delivered by invested caregivers - NOT bare kin count or genealogical presence. Four relatives who live far away and do not share the daily load do not satisfy the parameter; what the infant and mother expect is dependable, hands-on, repeated care from a stable surround.
eea_parameters.confidence_note: Grade, rubric v2 (6 Nov 2026): tested many times. Shared infant care is observed in many forager populations by separate field teams (Hadza, Efe, Aka, !Kung, Agta, Pume); the share of care varies widely. The 'cooperative breeder' reading and the calorie argument stay Hrdy's interpretation. In 15,696 UK infants, care by kin (odds ratio 0.61) and formal daycare (0.68) as the main weekday care went with lower odds of developmental delay at 9 months, and an infant whose mother had none of the six kinds of help and company measured (care by kin in working hours, seeing her own mother, time with friends, other mothers to talk to, family she could count on for money, people at the birth) had about eight times the odds of delay of one whose mother had the most of all six (Waynforth 2024).

eea_parameters.name: Caregiver continuity and reliability (present, not merely countable)
eea_parameters.eea_baseline: The ancestral infant developed within a web of stable, repeatedly-present attachment figures whose availability could be counted on. Attachment is not a single dyadic bond but secure attachment to one or more trusted caretakers - Bowlby's design refined by Hrdy to plural, reliably-present figures - and human infants are equipped with traits (cuteness, prolonged eye contact, social smiling, differentiated cries) for recruiting and holding the attention of multiple potential caretakers. Crucially, maternal commitment itself is contingent and reliability-sensitive: for a cooperatively breeding mammal, the capacity to conceive is only part of the equation; the mother must be able to carry through to rearing independence, which she assesses against the dependable support actually available. Touch is part of this continuity - the infant evolved to expect near-continuous skin contact (carried, held, co-sleeping), a sense developed first in utero and serving as a primary regulatory channel. The expectation is not a list of relatives but caregivers who are reliably, physically present across time.
eea_parameters.modern_default: Modern caregiving is frequently discontinuous and rotating: paid daycare with staff turnover, sequential and inconsistent caregivers, geographically dispersed or intermittently-available kin, and reduced continuous body contact (separate sleeping, stroller and crib time, scheduled rather than on-demand holding). Caregivers may be nominally present (counted on paper) yet not reliably, responsively available in the moment-to-moment way the regulatory system expects.
eea_parameters.gap_statement: The mismatch is between caregiver reliability/continuity as an experienced, present regulatory input and a modern environment that often supplies caregivers who are countable but not dependably present. Because maternal investment and infant attachment are both calibrated to perceived caregiver reliability (M9, R1), low continuity is not neutral: it degrades the secure-base scaffolding and the touch-mediated regulation the infant evolved to expect, even when the number of caregivers on paper looks adequate.
eea_parameters.resolution_unit: Reliable, present caregiver supply - responsive caregivers actually and repeatedly available across time, including continuity of body contact - NOT a count of designated or genealogically-related caregivers. The naive reading (enough named caregivers exist) misleads; what regulates the infant is dependable presence.
eea_parameters.confidence_note: All supporting extractions for the continuity/reliability claim are graded theoretical (Hrdy/Bowlby interpretive synthesis); the touch items are 296 (theoretical) and 294 (cross_species, Harlow/Suomi). The row is graded argued, not yet tested. The claim that maternal commitment is contingent on perceived reliable support (281, 402) and that attachment is to plural trusted figures (276) is well-grounded; the specific operationalization of 'continuity' as a measured construct is not pinned to a number, hence eea_value is null and the parameter is qualitative.

eea_parameters.name: Selection rule / "shuffle algorithm" (choice-driven; homophily + cooperation + reciprocity; kinship not main glue)
eea_parameters.eea_baseline: Who you lived alongside was not assigned by birth or fixed institution but produced by an ongoing, choice-driven assortment process operating across frequent residential reshuffling. In Hadza camps this "algorithm" had recurring structure: (1) homophily - co-residence was more likely between people similar in age, height, weight, body fat, and handgrip strength; (2) strong reciprocity - naming was near-symmetric, with an ego roughly 37-51x (point ~44x) more likely to name an alter who named them; (3) cooperator assortment - cooperators clustered with cooperators, an association extending out to two degrees of separation in gift networks; plus transitivity and geographic decay. Crucially, kinship was NOT the main glue: people actively sorted on disposition and reciprocity, not primarily on relatedness. The output was a camp continually re-composed of preferred, reciprocating, similarly-cooperative partners.
eea_parameters.modern_default: Group membership is overwhelmingly assigned rather than self-assorted: workplaces, school classes, residential buildings, and algorithmically-curated feeds place you among people you did not choose and who did not choose you. Where modern matching exists (dating apps, professional networks, recommender feeds), the optimization target is engagement, novelty, or proximity-of-the-moment - not durable mutual reciprocity, demonstrated cooperativeness, or transitive trust within a personally-known group. The ancestral feedback loop (you preferentially co-reside with people who reciprocate your investment and who others vouch for, observed directly over time) is largely absent; assortment on cooperation is replaced by assortment on platform metrics or institutional convenience.
eea_parameters.gap_statement: The EEA delivered a continuous, agency-rich sorting process that filtered one's immediate social world toward reciprocating, cooperative, vouched-for partners - kinship was secondary. The modern environment inverts this: membership in one's daily groups is mostly imposed (employer, building, algorithm), and the explicit matching systems that do exist optimize for engagement/novelty rather than reciprocity and demonstrated cooperation. The result is reduced control over WHO populates one's social field, weaker assortment on actual cooperativeness, and loss of the transitive-reputation signal that let ancestral humans cluster with trustworthy reciprocators out to two degrees. The mismatch is not "fewer people" but a broken selection rule: the inputs the ancestral algorithm ran on (mutual choice, observed reciprocity, cooperator reputation) are no longer the primary determinants of who one lives and works among.
eea_parameters.confidence_note: Shuffle algorithm now grounded in Apicella 2012 full text: trait homophily, strong reciprocity (44.2x campmate / 14.3x gift), and social distance as important as genetic relatedness (kinship not the sole glue). Single Hadza population; kept thin.

eea_parameters.name: Within-camp kin fraction (low; campmates mostly unrelated)
eea_parameters.eea_baseline: A person's residential camp/band was NOT a clan of close relatives. Across forager societies the typical residential group (~25-50 people, ~28 adults) was composed mostly of individuals to whom the focal person was not closely related: primary/first-order kin (parents, siblings, offspring) made up only a small minority of co-residents (under 10% of a residential camp; Apicella et al. 2012, ext 601), and most campmates were unrelated or only distantly related. Because residence was bilocal/sex-egalitarian (couples lived with both the husband's and the wife's kin over time) and camps reshuffled frequently, genetic relatedness within a camp was low. The practical consequence: the durable social glue holding a camp together was NOT shared genes. The bonds that mattered, and that were conserved across the constant churn, were reciprocal, trust-based, reputation-tracked relationships between individuals who chose each other, not kin ties imposed by birth.

eea_value.source_caveat: Low within-camp relatedness: Hill et al. 2011 (PMID 21393537, 32-society co-residence census) is in Cor as work 172, background tier (ext 683); Dyble et al. 2015 (PMID 25977551) is in Cor as work 176, background tier (ext 687). The under-10 percent primary-kin figure is verbatim in Apicella et al. 2012 (work 115, core, ext 601) and Smith et al. 2018 gives primary kin per camp (work 116, core, ext 605); both are Hadza, so the figure is Hadza-anchored. Camp size range is illustrative.
eea_value.relatedness_qualitative: low; most campmates unrelated or distantly related

eea_parameters.modern_default: Modern social environments invert the ancestral pattern in two opposite directions at once. (1) The family one is biologically related to is now small and, for about two in three adults, not all within reach (in the US, of adults with a living parent or grown child, three in four have one within 30 miles, about a third have all of them that near, and 13 percent share a home with one; Choi et al. 2020, ext 4204), and often the ONLY kin one regularly co-resides with, so the kin one has are concentrated in a tiny stable household rather than diffused through a larger chosen group. (2) The larger groups one spends daily life inside (workplace, neighborhood, online networks, institutions) are composed of effectively unrelated strangers, but unlike the ancestral camp these groupings are NOT self-assembled through mutual choice, reciprocity, and reputation tracking; membership is assigned by employment, address, or platform. The result is that 'who you live and work among' is no longer the output of a relationship-selection process; it is administratively or commercially determined, and the unrelated people around you are frequently strangers you did not choose and do not reciprocally track.
eea_parameters.gap_statement: The ancestral signal was: 'the group around me is mostly unrelated people I (or my band) actively chose and continuously vetted through reciprocity and reputation; kinship is not what holds us together, the relationships are.' The modern signal is degraded on the selection axis: the unrelated people around us are still mostly unrelated (that part matches), but they are assigned rather than chosen, and the reciprocity/reputation machinery that turned unrelated campmates into durable trusted allies is largely absent or shallow. Mechanisms M3 (bonding) and M11 (cooperation/alliance) evolved expecting that low kin-relatedness would be compensated by self-selected, reciprocal, reputation-anchored dyads. Modernity delivers the low relatedness WITHOUT the compensating chosen-and-vetted dyadic structure, so the mechanisms fire in a world of unrelated-but-also-unbonded co-residents, which is a key part of why being surrounded by people can still register as social isolation.
eea_parameters.confidence_note: Grade, rubric v2 (6 Nov 2026): tested many times. Low relatedness within camps comes from a 32-society co-residence census (Hill et al. 2011) and is repeated by separate teams in Hadza, Agta and BaYaka (Apicella et al. 2012; Dyble et al. 2015); the under-10-percent primary-kin figure is Hadza-anchored.

eea_parameters.name: Mixed-age child playgroups as developmental input
eea_parameters.eea_baseline: Ancestral children developed social competence largely through self-organized, free, physically-active play with a mixed-age band of other children - younger and older mixed together - rather than under continuous adult supervision or in age-segregated peer cohorts. Rough-and-tumble and pretend play during the juvenile period is a dedicated developmental input: in the mammalian design, play is a distinct emotional system (Panksepp's PLAY) and play experience physically tunes the maturing prefrontal cortex, refining the circuits that later dampen the amygdala and support social reciprocity, partner discrimination, and emotional regulation. Critically, the AMOUNT and quality of play partners matters: animals raised with more play partners show progressively greater play experience and corresponding PFC development, and even the untreated playmates of more-playful partners develop greater cortical thickness - play is a partnered input, so a richer multi-partner (and, in the human case, multi-age) play environment is the expected calibrating stimulus.
eea_parameters.modern_default: Modern childhood compresses or eliminates free mixed-age play: age-segregated grade cohorts and daycare, adult-structured and supervised activities, indoor screen-based leisure, reduced unsupervised outdoor roaming, and safety norms that discourage rough-and-tumble. Children spend far less time in self-directed, physically-active, mixed-age peer play than the developmental window evolved to expect.
eea_parameters.gap_statement: The mismatch is between mixed-age, self-organized, physically-active play as the evolved calibrating input for the juvenile prefrontal cortex (M4, embedded in the alloparental child-minding network, M9) and a modern environment that supplies age-segregated, adult-structured, often sedentary substitutes. In rats, play with partners shapes the developing cortex (Pellis & Pellis 2009, ext 212, 220). Cor reads reduced free play in children as a missing developmental input. In children, general risky outdoor play (13 studies) and places that allow risky play (21 studies) went with better physical, mental, social and cognitive outcomes in a review of 74 studies (Ramsden et al. 2026), and children who played adventurously more had slightly fewer internalising symptoms and more positive affect (Dodd, Nesbit and FitzGibbon 2023).
eea_parameters.resolution_unit: Self-directed, mixed-age, physically-active free play actually engaged in - partnered play experience - NOT adult-structured activities, solitary screen play, or scheduled lessons that occupy time without delivering the rough-and-tumble, role-reversal, peer-negotiated input the circuits expect.
eea_parameters.confidence_note: Grade, rubric v2 (6 Nov 2026): tested many times. Mixed-age child playgroups are documented across forager societies in two systematic reviews (Lew-Levy et al. 2017, 2018). The label covers the ancestral value only: the claim that age mixing shapes development rests on rat work and is untested in humans. In monkeys, isolates recovered with younger partners (ext 542). A review of tests of pretend play found weak and inconsistent evidence that it causes the developmental gains credited to it (Lillard et al. 2013, ext 762); the tests it reviews are mostly adult-led play training in preschools, which is not the self-organised play this row describes.

Each of these is built around neural complexities that are only provisionally understood. Sexual urges are mediated by specific brain circuits and chemistries that are quite distinct for males and females but appear to share some components such as the physiological and psychological effects of oxytocin, which also promotes maternal motivation.
